proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\psi_*=\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\).  All probability orders below are uniform over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and are conditional on the deterministic signal and mask whenever the cited result is conditional.  The replacement of \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\) includes \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}subgaussian\mbox{-}noise}\); the structured dependency corrections expose that condition in every cited concentration or truncation step.

First verify that the new envelope supplies the small parameters used by the already established native-optimizer lemmas.  By \(\mathrm{ass:penalty\mbox{-}level}\), for a constant \(C_0<\infty\),
\[
 \sqrt n\,\ell_n+\lambda\le C_0\sqrt n\,\ell_n.
\]
Consequently, \(\mathrm{ass:signal\mbox{-}window\mbox{-}envelope}\) gives, with
\(\rho_n=(\sqrt n\,\ell_n+\lambda)/\psi_*\),
\[
 \rho_n\ell_n^2
 \le \frac{C_0\sqrt n\,\ell_n^3}
 {\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})}
 =\frac{C_0\ell_n}{\omega_n(\ell_n+H^{1/4})}
 \le\frac{C_0}{\omega_n}=o(1).
\tag{1}
\]
In particular, \(\rho_n=o(1)\), which is the spectral-gap and active-resolvent requirement in \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}active\mbox{-}resolvent}\).  The same bound is the small-subspace perturbation condition used by \(\mathrm{lem:preperiod\mbox{-}reconstruction\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}lag\mbox{-}covariance}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:fitted\mbox{-}curvature\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}stability}\).  Moreover,
\[
 \zeta_n:=\frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_*^2}
 \le
 \frac{\sqrt H}{\omega_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})^2}
 \le \omega_n^{-2}=o(1).
\tag{2}
\]
Thus the second-order aggregate and fitted-curvature requirements also hold.  Equations (1)--(2) explicitly recheck the sufficient rate conditions; they do not assert that this envelope is necessary or sharp.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:neighborhood\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}coupling}\) to obtain
\[
 \left|\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}\right|
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \ell_n^4\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_*^2}+n^{-3/2}\right\}\right].
\tag{3}
\]
On the simultaneous active event supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}active\mbox{-}resolvent}\), \(\mathrm{lem:native\mbox{-}implicit\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}expansion}\) gives the exact linear term \(\ell_{it}\), including its negative donor--pretreatment overlap, the declared quadratic term \(q_{it}\), and the cubic, polar/regularization, and scalar-resolvent remainders.  Averaging and using \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}variance}\) and \(\mathrm{def:quadratic\mbox{-}drift}\) identifies the first two averages as \(L\) and \(Q\).  The centered aggregation in \(\mathrm{lem:centered\mbox{-}quadratic\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}higher\mbox{-}aggregate}\), together with (3), therefore yields
\[
 \frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})
 =L+Q+R_{\mathrm{agg}},
\tag{4}
\]
\[
 |Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\ell_n^4}{\psi_*\sqrt n}\right),
 \qquad
 |R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \ell_n^4\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_*^2}+n^{-3/2}\right\}\right].
\tag{5}
\]
This proves the native transfer and aggregate expansion, including the stated composition of \(R_{\mathrm{agg}}\).

Next, \(\mathrm{lem:preperiod\mbox{-}reconstruction\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}lag\mbox{-}covariance}\) gives
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{fit}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n),
\tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 \Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{m}}+\frac{\log n}{m}
 +\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2\right).
\tag{7}
\]
The fitted singular-space differentiation in \(\mathrm{lem:fitted\mbox{-}curvature\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}stability}\) then gives
\[
 |\widehat B_2-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt n}{\psi_*^2}
 +\frac{\Delta_\gamma}{\psi_*}\right),
 \qquad
 \sum_{j=1}^N\|\widehat w_{j\cdot}-w_{j\cdot}\|_2^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2).
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (3)--(8) prove every raw conclusion of the theorem.

It remains to compare the errors to the oracle standard error.  By \(\mathrm{ass:variance\mbox{-}nondegeneracy}\), \(s^{-1}\le C\sqrt{nH}\).  Hence (5) and (8) imply
\[
 \frac{|Q-B_2|}{s}
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{\psi_*}\right),
\tag{9}
\]
\[
 \frac{|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|}{s}
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_*^2}
 +\frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{n}\right),
\tag{10}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{|\widehat B_2-B_2|}{s}
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_*^2}
 +\frac{\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}}{\psi_*}\right).
\tag{11}
\]
The window-length and balanced-growth assumptions imply \(H\le Cn\).  The new envelope therefore gives
\[
 \frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{\psi_*}
 \le\frac{\ell_n^2\sqrt H}
 {\omega_n\sqrt n(\ell_n+H^{1/4})}
 \le\frac{C\ell_n^2}{\omega_n n^{1/4}}=o(1),
\tag{12}
\]
while the first term in (10) and (11) is \(o(1)\) by (2), and
\[
 \frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{n}\le\frac{C\ell_n^4}{\sqrt n}=o(1).
\tag{13}
\]
Because \(m\ge c_Sn\), (6)--(7) yield
\[
 \Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n).
\tag{14}
\]
Thus the final term in (11) satisfies
\[
 \frac{\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}}{\psi_*}
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\ell_n^2\sqrt H}{\psi_*}\right)
 \le O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\sqrt H}{\omega_n\sqrt n(\ell_n+H^{1/4})}\right)
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{15}
\]
Equations (9)--(15) prove oracle-scale negligibility under the sharpened sufficient envelope.

Finally, \(\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}signal}\) gives \(\psi_*\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\).  Since restriction to rows and columns is multiplication by contractions, singular-value monotonicity gives \(\sigma_r(M^{it})\le\sigma_r(M)=\psi\), hence \(\psi_*\le\psi\).  This proves the stated local-to-global comparison.  The older displayed condition in the target also implies the sharpened condition: if \(\psi\ge n^{1/2+\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^8\), then
\[
 \frac{\psi_*}{\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})}
 \ge
 c_{\mathrm{loc}}n^\eta\ell_n^6
 \frac{H^{1/4}}{\ell_n+H^{1/4}}
 \ge
 \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}n^\eta\ell_n^6}{\ell_n+1}
 \longrightarrow\infty,
\tag{16}
\]
where \(H\ge1\).  Hence the theorem's displayed older sufficient implication follows a fortiori, while (1)--(15) establish the materially weaker rate-exact sufficient envelope for the enlarged post-edit class.

Work under an arbitrary sequence \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), conditionally on \((M,\Omega)\).  The replacement of \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\) makes the conditional sub-Gaussian exponential-moment condition a member property, so the established conditional score central limit theorem is available on the same class.

On \(G\times W\), \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}start\mbox{-}mask}\) gives \(A_{it}=1\), and \(\mathrm{ass:causal\mbox{-}consistency}\) therefore gives \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=Y_{it}(1)\).  Comparing the definitions of the estimator and the causal target, rather than defining the target through the estimator, gives the exact equality
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau-\tau
 &=\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}
 \left[Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}-\widehat M_{it}
       -\{Y_{it}(1)-M_{it}\}\right]\\
 &=-\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it}).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
The untreated-factor assumption identifies \(M_{it}\) as the conditional untreated signal component; equation (17) is the required observed-law-to-causal bridge for the declared realized cohort-window contrast.

By \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\),
\[
 \frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})
 =L+Q+R_{\mathrm{agg}}.
\tag{18}
\]
Using \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=\widehat\tau+\widehat B_2\), add and subtract \(B_2\) in (17)--(18) to obtain
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau
 =-L-(Q-B_2)-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+(\widehat B_2-B_2).
\tag{19}
\]
Equations (9)--(15) in the proof of the native-transfer theorem show, under the sharpened envelope that defines \(\mathcal P_n\), that each of the last three terms in (19) is \(o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), uniformly over the class.  Therefore
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s).
\tag{20}
\]

For variance consistency, let \(d_{j\cdot}=\widehat w_{j\cdot}-w_{j\cdot}\).  Define the \(T\times T\) banded matrices
\[
 (\Gamma_q)_{uv}=1\{|u-v|\le q\}\gamma(v-u),
 \qquad
 (\widehat\Gamma_q)_{uv}=1\{|u-v|\le q\}\widehat\gamma(v-u).
\tag{21}
\]
The definitions of \(s^2\) and \(\widehat V\) imply
\[
 s^2=\sum_{j=1}^Nw_{j\cdot}^{\top}\Gamma_qw_{j\cdot},
 \qquad
 \widehat V=\sum_{j=1}^N(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot})^{\top}
 \widehat\Gamma_q(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot}).
\tag{22}
\]
Conditional sub-Gaussianity bounds \(|\gamma(h)|\) uniformly by conditional Cauchy--Schwarz.  Since \(q\) is fixed, the maximum absolute row-sum bound and the definition of \(\Delta_\gamma\) give
\[
 \|\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(1),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le(2q+1)\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{23}
\]
Expanding (22), applying Cauchy--Schwarz in the direct sum of the \(N\) row spaces, and using (23) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat V-s^2|
 &\le \|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|w\|_F^2
   +2\|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|w\|_F\|d\|_F
   +\|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|d\|_F^2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{24}
\]
The established \(\mathrm{lem:score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\) gives \(\|w\|_F^2=O(s^2)\), while the fitted-weight conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\) gives \(\|d\|_F^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\).  Dividing (24) by the positive quantity \(s^2\), whose lower bound is supplied by \(\mathrm{ass:variance\mbox{-}nondegeneracy}\), proves
\[
 \frac{|\widehat V-s^2|}{s^2}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{25}
\]
In particular, \(\widehat V>0\) with probability tending uniformly to one.

By \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}clt}\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{26}
\]
Normal symmetry gives the same assertion for \(-L/s\).  Combining (20), (25), and (26) by conditional Slutsky's argument gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P\!\left(
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau}{\sqrt{\widehat V}}
 \le z\,\middle|\,M,\Omega\right)-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{27}
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), evaluate (27) at the continuity points \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\).  By the definition of \(\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\), this yields
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
 \mathbb P_P\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\mid M,\Omega\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\tag{28}
\]

The argument is scalar and allows \(H\to\infty\), but it neither proves event-time bands nor changes the fixed known rank.  The class comparison is also restricted as claimed: Choi--Yuan impose independent cell noise, their stated subgroup-size regime, and separate loading and rate conditions, whereas \(\mathcal P_n\) permits fixed-range serial dependence but imposes balanced dimensions, fixed rank and incoherence, \(g\asymp n\), the common-start mask, and singleton target-local fits.  Hence neither full class contains the other.  On the explicit intersection with Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v), \(q=0\), and \(H=1\), the published-reduction proposition gives the one-date reduction.  This proves the revised comparison sentence without claiming equality or nesting of the two full classes.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every sequence in \(\mathcal P_n\), including sequences with \(H\to\infty\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\), and the primitive conditional block-dependence and score-diffuseness conditions yield \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P_P\{(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\le z\mid M,\Omega\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). Consequently, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb P_P\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\mid M,\Omega\}\to1-\alpha\). This is an extension of the balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup Choi--Yuan regime along the serial-dependence and growing-window axes, under a strengthened uniform class. Neither full class contains the other, and the \(q=0,H=1\) reduction is asserted only on the intersection with Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current final sentence claims a strict extension of the full Choi--Yuan class, but the two classes are incomparable. The corrected claim limits the reduction to the explicit intersection with Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v) and describes only the serial-dependence and growing-window extensions under this note's strengthened uniform class.

proposed.name: omegaenv
proposed.role: indexes slack in the sufficient local-signal envelope

proposed_core_edits.reason: The rate-exact sufficient envelope requires an explicitly declared deterministic divergence sequence.

proposed.condition:
The minimum local signal satisfies
\[
 \psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}
 \ge \omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2\bigl(\ell_n+H^{1/4}\bigr).
\]

novel.justification: This is a sufficient rather than sharp envelope. It gives threshold order \(\omega_n n^{3/4}\ell_n^2\) when \(H\asymp n\) and \(\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^3\) when \(H\) is fixed, while retaining the native estimator and its feasible correction.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The discharged perturbation bounds require exactly \(\rho_n\ell_n^2=o(1)\) and \(\ell_n^4n\sqrt H/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2=o(1)\); the former global envelope contained unnecessary polynomial and logarithmic slack.

proposed.name: Uniform deterministic-MNAR weak-signal class
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P_n:P_n\text{ governs }(M_n,\epsilon_n,Y_n(0),Y_n(1),A_n,G_n,S_n,W_n)\text{ and satisfies every member property listed for }\mathcal P_n\text{ at index }n\}\)

proposed_core_edits.reason: Conditional truncation and conditional third-moment arguments already use the approved conditional exponential-moment bound, so it must be a member property of the theorem's class.

proposed.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and \((i,t)\in G\times W\), put \(e_{it}=E^{it}_{it}\) and \(E_{it}=P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\). With probability tending to one, every minimizer in the definition of the native estimator has
\[
 \|Z^{it}-M^{it}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\sqrt n\,\ell_n,
 \qquad
 \frac{\sqrt n\,\ell_n+\lambda}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}=o(1),
\]
simultaneously over at most \(gH=O(n^2)\) targets. On this event,
\[
 \sigma_r(Z^{it})\ge\frac12\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}},
 \qquad \sigma_{r+1}(Z^{it})<\lambda,
\]
and every convex minimizer satisfies
\[
 \widetilde M^{it}=\mathcal P_r(Z^{it})-\lambda\mathsf S_r(Z^{it}),
 \qquad \mathsf S_r(Z)=U_r(Z)V_r(Z)^{\top}.
\]
The missing-coordinate equation has derivative
\[
 1-h_{it}+O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n\,\ell_n+\lambda}
 {\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right),
 \qquad h_{it}=O(\mu r/n),
\]
whose reciprocal is uniformly bounded. Hence its target value is unique, so the conclusion applies to the minimizer selected by the fixed measurable rule.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The simultaneous conditional spectral-noise bound uses the approved conditional exponential-moment assumption; the dependency must be explicit.

proposed.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the native and neighborhood-noise-replaced scalar resolvents satisfy
\[
 \left|\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}\right|
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \ell_n^4\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
 +n^{-3/2}\right\}\right].
\]
In the common-start local chart the native and auxiliary inputs, and hence their selected target values, agree identically whenever \(S\cap\mathcal N_q(t)=\varnothing\); because \(q\) is fixed and \(W\) is consecutive after \(S\), only \(O(q)\) target dates can contribute.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The conditional neighborhood-coupling tail bound uses the approved conditional exponential-moment condition.

proposed.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the local quadratic kernels lift to a symmetric matrix \(A_n\) on the common ambient observed array such that
\[
 Q-B_2=\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon
 -\mathbb E[\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon\mid M,\Omega]
\]
and
\[
 |Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\sqrt n}\right).
\]
The cubic, polar/regularization, scalar-resolvent, and native--auxiliary terms in the signed aggregate obey
\[
 |R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \ell_n^4\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
 +n^{-3/2}\right\}\right].
\]
These are centered aggregate bounds; they do not follow by summing pointwise absolute errors.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The centered quadratic-form proof explicitly conditions, truncates, and uses conditional moments; its approved tail premise must be declared.

proposed.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the pretreatment rank-\(r\) fit satisfies
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{fit}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n).
\]
For every fixed \(|h|\le q\), decomposition into the oracle residual-product average, two signal-error cross terms, and a quadratic signal-error term gives
\[
 |\widehat\gamma(h)-\gamma(h)|
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{m}}+\frac{\log n}{m}
 +\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2\right),
\]
and hence the same bound holds for \(\Delta_\gamma\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Conditional concentration of residual products and signal-error cross terms uses the approved conditional exponential-moment condition.

proposed.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), first express all perturbation bounds through \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}=\inf_{(i,t)\in G\times W}\sigma_r(M^{it})\). The native and neighborhood-replaced fits satisfy \(|(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\{\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+n^{-3/2}\})\), and the native estimator obeys \((gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})=L+Q+R_{\mathrm{agg}}\), where \(|Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4/(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\sqrt n))\), \(|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\{\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+n^{-3/2}\})\), \(\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n)\), \(\Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{\log n/m}+\log n/m+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2)\), \(|\widehat B_2-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+\Delta_\gamma/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}})\), and \(\sum_i\|\widehat w_{i\cdot}-w_{i\cdot}\|_2^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\). The term \(R_{\mathrm{agg}}\) contains the cubic, penalty, and native-transfer components fixed by its definition. Since \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\le\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\le\psi\), substitution changes only constants. Under \(\psi\ge n^{1/2+\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^8\), the corresponding remainder-to-standard-error ratios are bounded by terms of orders \(\ell_n^4\sqrt H/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\), \(\ell_n^4n\sqrt H/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2\), \(\ell_n^4\sqrt H/n\), and \(\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\), all \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).
proposed.justification: The theorem establishes the previously missing bridge from a conditionally independent neighborhood-replaced proof device to a second-order expansion of the native masked convex optimizer.
proposed.gap: The new scalar active-manifold resolvent and centered ambient-kernel argument are not delivered by independent-noise MNAR completion or fully observed leave-neighbor PCA.
proposed.consumer: The theorem certifies that feasible correction and studentization apply to the estimator already used for the SEC Tick Size Pilot panel.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem's declared basis must expose the conditional tail premise used by its concentration and truncation lemmas.

proposed.statement: For every sequence in \(\mathcal P_n\), including sequences with \(H\to\infty\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\), and the primitive conditional block-dependence and score-diffuseness conditions yield \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P_P\{(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\le z\mid M,\Omega\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). Consequently, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb P_P\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\mid M,\Omega\}\to1-\alpha\). This is an extension of the balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup Choi--Yuan regime along the serial-dependence and growing-window axes, under a strengthened uniform class. Neither full class contains the other, and the \(q=0,H=1\) reduction is asserted only on the intersection with Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v).
proposed.justification: Native expansion, feasible curvature correction, covariance consistency, and fitted-weight stability turn the oracle score limit into implementable sustained-effect inference.
proposed.gap: Prior one-date completion and missing-factor HAC results do not give this corrected growing-window law for the native estimator.
proposed.consumer: The interval supports a scalar reanalysis of the SEC Tick Size Pilot's average sustained liquidity effect over the realized cohort and post window.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This synchronizes the narrowed comparison claim, its intersection-reduction dependency, and the conditional tail premise used by the uniform score law.

proposed.comparator_claim: Under Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v), subgroup nuclear-norm completion permits one-date inference for imputed entries with independent cell noise and its stated subgroup-size and loading regimes.
proposed.matched_by: The published-reduction proposition only on the explicit class intersection; the feasible-window theorem adds serial dependence and growing windows under this note's strengthened uniform class.

proposed.comparator_claim: Leave-neighbor-out analysis gives weak-factor principal-component normality under dependent noise in a fully observed matrix.
Auxiliary leave-one-out estimators are asymptotically equivalent to the feasible nuclear-norm-based estimator without sample splitting.
Residual HAC estimators consistently estimate covariance matrices for weak-factor tensor loading scores with missing observations.
Convex and nonconvex matrix-completion solutions are tightly coupled under independent random entry sampling.
Double-debiased matrix completion yields confidence intervals for general linear forms under random entry sampling.
Residual block bootstrap confidence intervals cover fixed-cell treatment effects under weakly dependent factor errors.
Adjusted principal components provide pointwise factor and loading inference with general missing observations and dependent errors.
Factor and loading limit distributions are derived under general missing-data patterns.
Bias-aware confidence intervals attain uniformly correct coverage over weak interactive effects for admissible regressors.
Analytically bias-corrected alternating maximization is asymptotically normal for regression coefficients under unbalanced interactive effects.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Choi--Yuan comparison is an intersection reduction plus extensions along selected axes, not a strict tightening or nesting of the full published class.

prose_updates.tldr: For a deterministic common-start missing block, the native one-missing-cell convex optimizer has a complete three-block tangent score and a serial rank-projection drift. Neighborhood replacement through the native fixed point, centered quadratic aggregation, residual finite-lag covariance estimation, and fitted Hessian and weight stability yield feasible uniform scalar Wald inference whenever \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\) with \(\omega_n\to\infty\). This is a sufficient envelope, not a sharp frontier.

project_justification.gap: Choi and Yuan's deterministic-MNAR result treats independent cell noise under its own subgroup-size, loading, and rate conditions, while dependent-noise factor and residual-HAC results do not control the implemented masked convex completion estimator at the shrinking standard-error scale of a growing causal window. The Choi--Yuan class and this note's strengthened uniform class are not nested.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a native-optimizer second-order expansion whose first differential retains donor-window, treated-pre, and negative donor-pre overlap terms and whose projector curvature is contracted against finite-lag covariance, with all errors controlled at the oracle window scale.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies that expansion, a feasible Hessian--lag covariance correction, an influence-weighted residual covariance estimator, an independent-row finite-range central limit theorem, and uniform Wald coverage under the rate-exact sufficient envelope \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\). The one-date Choi--Yuan reduction is stated only on the explicit intersection with their Conditions (i)--(v), while the separate exponent-indexed sharp-frontier question remains open.

sampling_model.units: Conditional on the signal, row laws factor across units. Within each row the centered process has common stationary covariance, fixed known dependence range \(q\), and a uniform conditional sub-Gaussian exponential-moment bound.
sampling_model.overlap: Donor and pretreatment factor Grams have explicit normalized eigenvalue bounds, and every target restriction retains a fixed positive fraction of the global signal. The proved proportional-cohort theorem assumes the sufficient local envelope \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\), which is \(\omega_n n^{3/4}\ell_n^2\) when \(H\asymp n\) and \(\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^3\) when \(H\) is fixed. Its score variance is of order \((nH)^{-1}\).

prose_updates.related_work: Choi and Yuan (2024) provide the deterministic-MNAR subgroup nuclear-norm and rank-projection architecture under independent cell noise and their stated subgroup-size, loading, and rate conditions. This note is an extension of their balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup regime along the serial-dependence and growing-window axes, under a strengthened uniform class; neither full class contains the other, and the formal one-date reduction is only on the explicit intersection with Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v). Choi and Yuan (2025) provide the fully observed leave-neighbor weak-factor precedent; the present proof transfers neighborhood replacement through the actual masked convex fixed point. Cen and Lam (2025) motivate residual HAC for missing-factor scores, whereas the present result contracts fitted rank-projection Hessians and aggregate influence weights against finite-lag covariance. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) supply only a backup coupling pattern and do not replace the estimator.
prose_updates.interpretation: The confidence interval concerns one scalar: the realized treated cohort's average sustained effect over the declared consecutive post window. For the SEC Tick Size Pilot reanalysis, it supports a cohort-window liquidity contrast after native completion and serial-curvature correction; it is not an event-time band.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Uniformity requires exact known fixed rank, fixed known dependence range, balanced dimensions, a proportional treated cohort, normalized donor and pretreatment Gram bounds, local-to-global signal comparability, conditional sub-Gaussian tails, and \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\). The proof uses a one-missing-coordinate common-start chart and fixed-range dependency-graph coloring. It does not establish larger missing local blocks, unknown rank, heterogeneous or long-range covariance, simultaneous event-time bands, or validity at the proportional-window spectral-noise boundary; the sufficient envelope is not claimed sharp.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved class conditions on exact known fixed rank, fixed known dependence range, conditionally independent rows, genuine within-row finite-range dependence, common stationary covariance, conditional sub-Gaussian tails, a fixed positive local-to-global signal ratio, a proportional treated cohort, bounded aspect ratios, and explicit donor and pretreatment restricted-Gram bounds. It covers growing windows under \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\omega_n\sqrt n\,\ell_n^2(\ell_n+H^{1/4})\), including \(H\asymp n\) at sufficient order \(\omega_n n^{3/4}\ell_n^2\) and the rank-one calibration \(\psi=n^{4/5}\). It does not claim that this is the sharp frontier, that its class contains the full Choi--Yuan class, or that \(q=0,H=1\) makes the classes identical. It does not cover simultaneous event-time bands, unknown rank, heterogeneous covariance, hidden-block identification, rank overprojection, or proportional-window inference arbitrarily close to signal order \(n^{1/2}\).

statement_notes.justification: The theorem transports the complete linear and quadratic expansion through the native masked optimizer and proves oracle-scale negligibility under the rate-exact sufficient local-signal envelope.
statement_notes.gap: Independent-noise MNAR completion and fully observed leave-neighbor PCA do not supply the native scalar resolvent, centered ambient quadratic kernel, or feasible serial-curvature stability needed at a growing-window standard-error scale.
statement_notes.consumer: The result certifies that the estimator used for the SEC Tick Size Pilot panel can be bias-corrected and studentized without replacing its native convex fit.

statement_notes.justification: Native expansion, feasible curvature correction, finite-lag covariance consistency, and fitted-weight stability yield uniform scalar Wald inference over the strengthened class.
statement_notes.gap: The result extends the balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup Choi--Yuan regime only along serial-dependence and growing-window axes; the full classes are incomparable, and the one-date reduction holds only on their explicit condition intersection.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) that also satisfies conditions (i)--(v) of Choi and Yuan (2024), Theorem 3.1.  Put \(W=\{t_0\}\), abbreviate \(A=A_{t_0}\) and \(B=B_S\), and define
\[
 \bar x_G=\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}x_i.
\]
The donor and pretreatment restricted-Gram assumptions give \(A\succ0\) and \(B\succ0\), so every inverse below exists.  By the definition of the oracle score and the complete-tangent lemma,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L
 &=\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}\ell_{i t_0}(R_{i t_0}\epsilon)\\
 &=\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}
       x_i^{\top}A^{-1}x_j\epsilon_{j,t_0}
   +\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{u\in S}
       f_{t_0}^{\top}B^{-1}f_u\epsilon_{iu}\\
 &\quad
   -\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}\sum_{u\in S}
       x_i^{\top}A^{-1}x_j
       f_{t_0}^{\top}B^{-1}f_u\epsilon_{ju}\\
 &=\mathcal D_n+\mathcal T_n-\mathcal O_n,
 \end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
 \mathcal D_n
 =\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}\bar x_G^{\top}A^{-1}x_j\epsilon_{j,t_0},
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_n
 =\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{u\in S}
       f_{t_0}^{\top}B^{-1}f_u\epsilon_{iu},
\]
and \(\mathcal O_n\) is the donor--pretreatment overlap score in the one-date curvature-and-overlap lemma.  In particular, the negative overlap is an exact part of the differential, rather than a term suppressed by definition.

Because \(q=0\), conditional block dependence says that distinct dates within a row are conditionally independent given \(M\); conditional row independence gives the same conclusion across distinct rows.  The common-start mask makes the three coordinate sets
\[
 C(t_0)\times\{t_0\},
 \qquad G\times S,
 \qquad C(t_0)\times S
\]
pairwise disjoint.  Conditional centering and common stationary covariance therefore imply that \(\mathcal D_n\), \(\mathcal T_n\), and \(\mathcal O_n\) are conditionally centered and mutually conditionally independent.  From \(A=\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}x_jx_j^{\top}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(\mathcal D_n\mid M,\Omega)
 &=\gamma(0)\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}
    \bigl(\bar x_G^{\top}A^{-1}x_j\bigr)^2\\
 &=\gamma(0)\bar x_G^{\top}A^{-1}
    \left(\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}x_jx_j^{\top}\right)
    A^{-1}\bar x_G\\
 &=\gamma(0)\bar x_G^{\top}A^{-1}\bar x_G.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Likewise, using \(B=\sum_{u\in S}f_uf_u^{\top}\) and independence of the \(g\) treated rows,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(\mathcal T_n\mid M,\Omega)
 &=\frac{\gamma(0)}{g^2}\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{u\in S}
   \bigl(f_{t_0}^{\top}B^{-1}f_u\bigr)^2\\
 &=\frac{\gamma(0)}g f_{t_0}^{\top}B^{-1}
   \left(\sum_{u\in S}f_uf_u^{\top}\right)
   B^{-1}f_{t_0}\\
 &=\frac{\gamma(0)}g f_{t_0}^{\top}B^{-1}f_{t_0}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consequently the variance of the two-component score is
\[
 V_{\mathrm{CY}}
 :=\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal D_n+\mathcal T_n\mid M,\Omega)
 =\gamma(0)\left\{
    \bar x_G^{\top}A^{-1}\bar x_G
    +\frac1g f_{t_0}^{\top}B^{-1}f_{t_0}
  \right\}.
\]

This is the variance displayed by Choi and Yuan, expressed in the present factor normalization.  To verify the equality, let
\[
 \bar U_G=\frac1g\sum_{i\in G}U_{i\cdot}^{\top}.
\]
The definitions \(X=UD^{1/2}\) and \(F=VD^{1/2}\) give
\[
 A=D^{1/2}\left(\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}
 U_{j\cdot}^{\top}U_{j\cdot}\right)D^{1/2},
 \qquad \bar x_G=D^{1/2}\bar U_G,
\]
and hence
\[
 \bar x_G^{\top}A^{-1}\bar x_G
 =\bar U_G^{\top}
  \left(\sum_{j\in C(t_0)}U_{j\cdot}^{\top}U_{j\cdot}\right)^{-1}
  \bar U_G.
\]
Similarly,
\[
 f_{t_0}^{\top}B^{-1}f_{t_0}
 =V_{t_0\cdot}
  \left(\sum_{u\in S}V_{u\cdot}^{\top}V_{u\cdot}\right)^{-1}
  V_{t_0\cdot}^{\top}.
\]
Thus \(V_{\mathrm{CY}}\) is exactly the sum of the donor-loading quadratic form and the group-size-scaled pretreatment-factor quadratic form appearing in the cited theorem.

The oracle-variance definition and the preceding conditional independence yield
\[
 s^2
 =\operatorname{Var}(L\mid M,\Omega)
 =V_{\mathrm{CY}}+operatorname{Var}(\mathcal O_n\mid M,\Omega).
\]
The one-date curvature-and-overlap lemma gives, uniformly on \(\mathcal P_n\),
\[
 \mathcal O_n=o_{\mathbb P}(s),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\mathcal O_n\mid M,\Omega)=O(n^{-2}),
 \qquad
 B_2=o_{\mathbb P}(s).
\]
Its variance comparison uses the declared nondegeneracy bound \(s^2\ge c_s/n\) at \(H=1\).  Therefore
\[
 0\le
 \frac{\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal O_n\mid M,\Omega)}{s^2}
 \le \frac{C n^{-2}}{c_s n^{-1}}
 =O(n^{-1})\longrightarrow0,
\]
and hence
\[
 \frac{V_{\mathrm{CY}}}{s^2}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{s^2}{V_{\mathrm{CY}}}\longrightarrow1.
\]

On the imposed intersection, the cited Choi--Yuan theorem applies and gives
\[
 \frac{\mathcal D_n+\mathcal T_n}{\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{CY}}}}
 \ \Rightarrow\ N(0,1).
\]
Combining this result with the exact score decomposition gives
\[
 \frac{L}{s}
 =\frac{\mathcal D_n+\mathcal T_n}{\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{CY}}}}
   \sqrt{\frac{V_{\mathrm{CY}}}{s^2}}
   -\frac{\mathcal O_n}{s}
 =Z_n+R_n,
\]
where
\[
 Z_n=\frac{\mathcal D_n+\mathcal T_n}{\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{CY}}}}
 \Rightarrow \mathcal N(0,1)
\]
and
\[
 R_n=
 \left(\sqrt{\frac{V_{\mathrm{CY}}}{s^2}}-1\right)Z_n
 -\frac{\mathcal O_n}{s}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
Indeed, convergence of \(Z_n\) to a proper distribution makes \(Z_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\), while the multiplier in parentheses converges to zero.  To verify the last distributional step without adding any further premise, let \(\Phi\) be the standard-normal distribution function.  For every \(x\in\mathbb R\) and \(\delta>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P(Z_n\le x-\delta)-\mathbb P(|R_n|>\delta)
 \le \mathbb P(Z_n+R_n\le x)
 \le \mathbb P(Z_n\le x+\delta)+\mathbb P(|R_n|>\delta).
\]
Taking lower and upper limits and then letting \(\delta\downarrow0\), continuity of \(\Phi\) gives \(L/s\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\).  Since \(B_2/s=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), the same sandwich argument shows that adding or subtracting the curvature drift does not change this limit.  This proves the estimator-and-limit reduction on the explicit intersection.  The argument has nowhere identified the two assumption classes: the final extension language refers only to retaining this intersection benchmark while allowing the present construction's serial-dependence and growing-window axes under its strengthened uniform assumptions.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Let \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) satisfy, in addition, conditions (i)--(v) of Choi and Yuan (2024), Theorem 3.1, and specialize to \(q=0\), \(H=1\), and \(W=\{t_0\}\). Then \(B_2=o_{\mathbb P}(s)\); the complete score \(L\) differs by \(o_{\mathbb P}(s)\) from the two-component Choi--Yuan score; the ratio of \(s^2\) to their displayed variance converges to one; and the resulting standardized leading score converges in distribution to \(\mathcal N(0,1)\). This is a reduction on the explicit intersection of the two sets of conditions, not an assertion that the Choi--Yuan model class and \(\mathcal P_n\) coincide. In this intersection-reduction sense, the construction is an extension of the balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup Choi--Yuan regime along the serial-dependence and growing-window axes, under a strengthened uniform class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The prior wording could be read as saying that the specializations \(q=0\) and \(H=1\) identify the full Choi--Yuan class with this note's class. The published conditions and the present strengthened uniform conditions are not identical, so the honest reduction is on their explicit intersection. The proposed statement preserves the estimator-and-limit reduction while making that restriction and the extension axes explicit.

Then \(B_2=o_{\mathbb P}(s)\); the complete score \(L\) differs by \(o_{\mathbb P}(s)\) from the two-component Choi--Yuan score; the ratio of \(s^2\) to their displayed variance converges to one; and the resulting standardized leading score converges in distribution to \(\mathcal N(0,1)\). This is a reduction on the explicit intersection of the two sets of conditions, not an assertion that the Choi--Yuan model class and \(\mathcal P_n\) coincide. In this intersection-reduction sense, the construction is an extension of the balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup Choi--Yuan regime along the serial-dependence and growing-window axes, under a strengthened uniform class.
proposed.justification: The reduction guards against changing the estimand or estimator while enlarging the serial-dependence and target-window regimes, and it now states the necessary intersection restriction explicitly.
proposed.gap: The published theorem supplies the benchmark only under its own conditions; this proposition proves the score, variance, overlap, and curvature map on the intersection with the present strengthened uniform class.
proposed.consumer: Applied users recover the published one-date procedure on the explicit intersection, without being told that the two underlying model classes coincide.
